slides.texte_overlay:
How to make a strong entrance
anywhere you go
Prepare before you arrive. Know who'll be there and one or two things to talk about. Preparation turns nerves into calm.
Breathe slowly at the door. One deep breath before walking in lowers your heart rate and relaxes your face. Then walk in.
Greet people with their name. "Hi Tom, good to see you." Names make people feel noticed straight away. Learn them and use them.
Bring good energy, not loud energy. A warm smile and an easy laugh are more welcoming than a big show. Warm beats loud.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Having interesting things to say makes walking in feel easy.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Having interesting things to say makes walking in feel easy.

slides.texte_overlay: Find the host and thank them. It's polite, it anchors you, and it often leads to your first introductions. Start there.
Stay curious once you're in. Ask questions, listen, introduce people. A strong entrance is followed by real attention.
